claims.claim: Kim Mohan, D&D's longest-serving editor, praises Ed Greenwood's prose for leaving the reader feeling that fifty words are held back behind every word given.
claims.source: Kim Mohan, quoted by Ramanan Sivaranjan reporting the D&D podcast interview, 2013
claims.quote: you feel like he’s holding fifty in reserve
claims.confidenceReason: the words reach us through a blogger's transcription of a podcast, not the recording

claims.claim: Mohan says that of every ten words Ed Greenwood supplies, three or four could probably have been kept back.

claims.quote: for every ten that he gives you he probably could

claims.claim: Stan!, who worked with Mohan for about ten years, says Mohan's job under whatever title was to set the editorial tone and mentor the staff.
claims.source: Stan! (Steven Brown), 50 Years in the Dungeon, 2025
claims.quote: always to set the editorial tone and mentor the staff

claims.claim: Stan! states that Mohan edited every edition of D&D from the original hardcovers to fifth-edition supplements.
claims.source: Stan! (Steven Brown), 50 Years in the Dungeon, 2025
claims.quote: worked on EVERY edition of D&D from the original hardcovers
claims.confidenceReason: a colleague's recollection, not a credits audit
